policies.title: Health and Safety Policy Statement of Intent

runs.t: {{company}} is {{about}}. The health, safety and welfare of our employees, subcontractors and anyone affected by our work is a core part of how we run the business, and the Director takes overall responsibility for it.
We will, so far as is reasonably practicable:

Comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 and all other legislation that applies to our work.
Provide and maintain safe systems of work, safe plant and equipment and a safe working environment, with the risks of our own trade assessed and controlled before work starts.
Assess the risks arising from our work and from the substances we use, and put suitable controls in place before work starts.
Provide the information, instruction, training and supervision our people need to work safely, including site inductions, toolbox talks and the trade qualifications relevant to our work.
Provide and maintain suitable personal protective equipment at no cost to our people.
Consult our workforce on matters affecting their health and safety and encourage the reporting of hazards, near misses and ill health without fear of blame.
Cooperate with principal contractors and clients, work to their site rules, and report anything that presents a risk.
Investigate accidents and near misses, learn from them and act on the findings.

Every person working for {{company}} has a duty to take reasonable care of themselves and others, to follow the method they have been briefed on, to use the equipment and PPE provided, and to stop and report any situation they believe to be unsafe.

We retain Safety Simplified Ltd as our competent health and safety adviser. This statement is reviewed at least annually, and sooner where the business, the work or the law changes, and is brought to the attention of all employees and subcontractors.
Policy statement

{{company}} is committed to conducting all aspects of its business honestly, ethically and with zero tolerance of bribery and corruption. This policy is designed to ensure compliance with the Bribery Act 2010 and applies to all directors, employees, and anyone working for or on behalf of the Company, including consultants, agency workers and subcontractors.

Under the Bribery Act 2010, individuals convicted of bribery face up to ten years' imprisonment and an unlimited fine. A company that fails to prevent bribery may face an unlimited fine and exclusion from tendering for public contracts.
Definitions

A bribe is a financial or other advantage offered, promised, given, requested or accepted to induce or reward the improper performance of a function or duty, or to influence a person in the performance of their duties. Facilitation payments and kickbacks are small payments made to secure or speed up a business favour or routine action; they are bribes and are prohibited.
The Company will not
Offer, give, request or accept bribes, kickbacks or facilitation payments of any kind
Make contributions of any kind with the purpose of gaining an improper commercial advantage
Provide gifts or hospitality intended to persuade anyone to act improperly, or to influence a public official in the performance of their duties
Make donations to charities, political parties or other organisations without Director approval
The Company will
Keep accurate internal records evidencing the business reason for payments to third parties
Encourage workers to raise concerns about suspected bribery at the earliest opportunity, through their manager, a Director, or the Whistleblowing Policy
Ensure that no one suffers detriment for raising a genuine concern, even if they are mistaken
Gifts and hospitality

Promotional gifts of low value and normal, proportionate business hospitality are permitted. Gifts with a value exceeding £25 must not be given or accepted without Director approval, and any gift refused on grounds of value must be reported. All corporate hospitality given or received must be transparent and approved in advance. Reasonable business travel and meal expenses while attending third-party conferences or seminars are exempt.
Non-compliance, monitoring and review

Breach of this policy by an employee may lead to disciplinary action in accordance with the Company's Disciplinary Policy. Breach by another organisation or individual will be assessed and appropriate action taken, which may include termination of the business relationship. This policy is reviewed annually, communicated to all workers, and all reported incidents are assessed by senior management.
Introduction

The Company encourages a culture of honesty and openness. Workers are often the first to know when something is wrong, and this policy exists so that concerns can be raised safely. The law (the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998, inserted into the Employment Rights Act 1996) protects workers who make a 'protected disclosure', a disclosure of information which, in the reasonable belief of the worker, is made in the public interest and tends to show wrongdoing.
Matters covered
A concern should be raised under this policy where a worker reasonably believes any of the following has occurred, is occurring, or is likely to occur:
A criminal offence, including bribery, fraud or the facilitation of tax evasion
Failure to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation
A miscarriage of justice
Danger to the health and safety of any individual
Damage to the environment
Anti-competitive conduct, including bid-rigging or cover pricing
Deliberate concealment of information relating to any of the above
Disclosure procedure
Concerns should be raised promptly with a manager so that appropriate action can be taken
If it is inappropriate to raise the concern with a manager, the worker should speak to a Director
Concerns will be investigated promptly and treated confidentially so far as possible; the worker will be informed of the outcome where appropriate
No worker will suffer any detriment for raising a genuine concern in accordance with this procedure, even if it turns out to be unfounded
Failure to follow this procedure may result in a disclosure losing its protected status; workers may seek guidance in confidence from a manager or Director

Where internal disclosure is not appropriate, workers may raise concerns with a relevant prescribed body (for example the Health and Safety Executive, the Environment Agency, HMRC, the Information Commissioner's Office or the Competition and Markets Authority).
Building safety concerns

This policy applies to concerns about building safety and compliance with the Building Regulations, including defective work, incomplete or damaged compartmentation and fire-stopping, incorrect or substituted products, inadequate fire precautions and risks to the structural safety of a building. Such concerns may be raised under this policy in confidence and are handled in line with the reporting arrangements in the Building Safety Policy.

policies.title: Prevention of the Facilitation of Tax Evasion Policy

runs.t: Policy statement

This policy sets out the Company's approach to its responsibilities under the Criminal Finances Act 2017, which makes it a corporate criminal offence to fail to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion by persons acting on the Company's behalf. The Company is committed to taking reasonable prevention procedures to prevent the facilitation of tax evasion, in the UK or abroad. This commitment extends to all employees and anyone acting on the Company's behalf.
Risk assessment
Given the nature of the business, the risks are assessed as low. The principal risks identified are:
Receiving an overpayment into the Company account and being asked to refund it, thereby 'cleaning' the money
Being asked by a supplier or subcontractor to pay in cash where it is known, or ought reasonably to be known, that the intention is not to declare the receipt for VAT or other tax purposes
Requests for payments to be split, redirected to third parties, or invoiced in a misleading way
Prevention procedures
Payments are made by bank transfer, card or cheque; cash payments are declined
Invoices and payments are checked against genuine supplies and appropriately skilled staff operate under management oversight
The Company's commitment to preventing the facilitation of tax evasion is communicated to staff, and relevant finance staff and senior colleagues are briefed on this law
Concerns of suspected facilitation must be reported to a Director immediately and may be raised under the Whistleblowing Policy; appropriate advice will be taken
Procedures under the HMRC guiding principles

The Company does not tolerate tax evasion, or the facilitation of tax evasion, in the UK or overseas, by anyone acting for it or on its behalf, including directors, employees, subcontractors, agency workers and suppliers, in accordance with the Criminal Finances Act 2017. The Company applies the following procedures, which follow the six guiding principles in HMRC guidance.
Risk assessment.

The Directors assess where the business could be exposed to the facilitation of tax evasion. The main areas are payments to subcontractors and labour providers, cash payments, and requests to change invoices or payment details. The assessment is reviewed annually and whenever the business changes.
Proportionality.

Procedures are proportionate to the size of the Company and the risks identified. Subcontractors are verified and paid under the Construction Industry Scheme, VAT is applied in line with HMRC rules, and payments are made by bank transfer against a valid invoice to an account in the supplier's own name.
Top level commitment.

The Directors are committed to preventing the facilitation of tax evasion and take responsibility for these procedures. No worker will suffer any detriment for refusing to take part in, or for reporting, suspected tax evasion.
Due diligence.

Proportionate checks are made on subcontractors, labour providers and suppliers before they are engaged and periodically afterwards, covering company and VAT registration, CIS status and bank details. Unusual requests, such as payment in cash, to a third party or to an overseas account, are referred to a Director before any payment is made.
Training and communication.

This policy is communicated to all workers at induction and through the Company's policy pack. Staff who deal with purchasing, payroll, accounts or the engagement of subcontractors are briefed on the warning signs and on how to report concerns, and records are kept.
Monitoring and review.

The Directors monitor compliance through checks on payments and supplier records. Concerns are reported to a Director or through the Whistleblowing Policy and are investigated. These procedures are reviewed at least annually, after any reported concern and when the law or guidance changes.
Review
Prevention procedures are monitored and enforced, and this policy is reviewed annually and whenever relevant formal guidance is published.
Policy statement

The Company is committed to competing fairly and complying fully with UK competition law, principally the Competition Act 1998 and the Enterprise Act 2002, enforced by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). Breaches can result in fines of up to 10% of worldwide turnover for the business, personal criminal liability for individuals involved in cartel activity (including imprisonment of up to five years), director disqualification for up to fifteen years, and exclusion from public sector tendering. The Company operates a zero-tolerance approach to anti-competitive conduct.
Prohibited conduct
No director, employee or person acting on behalf of the Company may enter into, or discuss with a competitor, any agreement, arrangement or understanding to:
Fix, stabilise or coordinate prices, rates, discounts, or terms and conditions
Rig bids or tenders in any way, including agreeing who will win a tender or coordinating bid content
Provide or obtain a cover price (a deliberately uncompetitive bid submitted to give the appearance of competition), the CMA treats cover pricing as a form of bid-rigging and it is strictly prohibited
Make or receive compensation payments connected to tendering outcomes
Share or allocate markets, customers, contracts or geographic areas
Exchange commercially sensitive information with competitors, including pricing, margins, bid intentions, costs, customer terms or strategic plans
Tendering rules

All bids and quotations must be prepared independently. Workers involved in estimating and tendering must not contact, or respond to contact from, a competitor regarding any tender. If the Company does not wish to bid for a contract, it will decline the invitation; it will never request or supply a cover price. Any approach from a competitor seeking to discuss prices, bids or markets must be rejected immediately and reported to a Director.
Trade associations and industry contact

Legitimate contact with competitors, for example through trade associations, industry bodies or joint health and safety forums, is permitted, but commercially sensitive matters must never be discussed. If such a discussion begins, workers must object, leave the meeting, report the matter to a Director, and record the objection and departure.
Reporting, training and review

Actual or suspected anti-competitive conduct must be reported to a Director without delay and may be raised under the Whistleblowing Policy; no one will suffer detriment for raising a genuine concern.

The Company is aware of the CMA's leniency programme and will take legal advice promptly if a potential infringement is identified. Staff involved in sales, estimating, tendering and procurement are briefed on this policy at induction and periodically thereafter, with records retained. This policy is reviewed annually.
Policy statement

The Company is committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion in employment, in the provision of services and throughout its supply chain. All people will be treated fairly and with respect, whether they are a job applicant, employee, worker, subcontractor, client or member of the public. The Company complies with the Equality Act 2010 and the Human Rights Act 1998.

No person will receive less favourable treatment or be disadvantaged on the grounds of the protected characteristics defined by the Equality Act 2010: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation. The Company also does not tolerate less favourable treatment on grounds such as trade union membership, part-time or fixed-term status, or spent convictions as defined by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.
Recruitment and selection

Recruitment, selection and promotion decisions are based on merit and made within the framework of this policy. Job descriptions and personnel specifications reflect genuine job requirements; vacancies are advertised in a consistent, non-discriminatory way; interview questions relate to the requirements of the job; and interviewing is carried out by more than one person where possible. Those involved in recruitment are trained in appropriate selection techniques. Reasonable adjustments will be made for disabled applicants and employees.
Conduct and standards of behaviour

Unacceptable behaviour includes: displaying or distributing offensive material; physical violence; verbal threats; swearing at others; persistent rudeness; isolating, ignoring or refusing to work with certain people; telling offensive jokes; name-calling; and any other victimising or harassing behaviour. These are disciplinary offences. It is no defence that offence was not intended, or that the recipient was oversensitive: it is the impact of the behaviour that counts.
Complaints and monitoring

All complaints of unlawful discrimination made by employees, clients or third parties will be investigated and action taken where appropriate; the complainant will be notified of the outcome. Complaints are monitored and lessons learned implemented. This policy is communicated to all workers, reviewed annually and updated in line with changes to legislation.
Policy statement

The Company is committed to providing a working environment free from sexual harassment. Sexual harassment is unlawful, will not be tolerated in any form, and may result in disciplinary action up to and including dismissal. This policy applies to all directors, employees, agency workers, subcontractors and others working for or on behalf of the Company.

This policy is written to comply with the Equality Act 2010 and the Worker Protection (Amendment of Equality Act 2010) Act 2023, which places a positive legal duty on employers to take reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of workers in the course of their employment, including harassment by third parties. The Company has regard to the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) technical guidance.
Definition

Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature which has the purpose or effect of violating a person's dignity, or creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment for them. It is the impact of the behaviour, not the intention behind it, that matters. Examples include sexual comments, jokes or innuendo; unwelcome physical contact; displaying or sharing images of a sexual nature, including via messaging apps; sexual advances or propositions; intrusive questions about a person's private or sex life; and wolf-whistling, catcalling or leering, including behaviour directed at members of the public from sites.
Scope

This policy applies in the workplace and any work-related setting, including construction sites, client premises, offices, welfare facilities, work vehicles, work-related social events, and online or telephone communications connected with work.
Preventative duty and risk assessment

The Company carries out and regularly reviews a risk assessment of factors that may increase the likelihood of sexual harassment, including lone working, male-dominated site environments, working on third-party premises, power imbalances, and alcohol at work-related events
This policy is communicated to all workers at induction and reinforced through toolbox talks and periodic refreshers
Clients, subcontractors and site visitors are made aware that harassment of our workers will not be tolerated
The working environment is monitored, including site culture and displayed material, and concerns are acted on promptly
Third-party harassment
Workers may experience sexual harassment from third parties such as clients, other contractors, suppliers or members of the public. Any such incident should be reported using the procedure below.

The Company will take action, which may include raising the matter with the third party's employer, removing workers from the environment, restricting the third party's contact with our workers, or terminating the business relationship.
Reporting, investigation and protection

Any worker who experiences or witnesses sexual harassment should report it to their manager, or to a Director if reporting to the manager is inappropriate. Reports may be made verbally or in writing, informally or formally, and will be treated seriously, promptly and as confidentially as possible. Complaints will be investigated impartially; where upheld against an employee, disciplinary action will be taken up to and including dismissal, and where a complaint concerns a subcontractor or supplier, services may be terminated. No worker will suffer detriment for raising a complaint in good faith or supporting an investigation; victimisation is itself a disciplinary offence.
Monitoring and review

This policy is reviewed annually and in line with legislative change or EHRC guidance. Records of training, toolbox talks and complaints are retained as evidence of compliance with the preventative duty.
Purpose and definition

The purpose of this policy is to ensure the workplace is free from bullying and harassment and to provide a framework for preventing and addressing incidents. Bullying is repeated and unreasonable behaviour directed towards an individual or group which creates a risk to health and safety. It can be physical, verbal or psychological, and includes intimidation, belittlement, humiliation, exclusion and abuse of power, whether in person, in writing or online.
Prohibition and prevention
The Company will not tolerate bullying or harassment in any form. All workers are expected to treat each other with respect, dignity and courtesy. The Company will:
Educate workers about the impact of bullying through induction and toolbox talks
Promote a workplace culture that values respect, diversity and inclusion
Encourage workers to report incidents to their manager or a Director
Provide support to workers who have been subjected to bullying behaviour
Investigation, consequences and non-retaliation

All complaints will be investigated promptly, thoroughly, impartially and as confidentially as possible, with all parties treated with respect and sensitivity. Anyone found to have engaged in bullying will be subject to disciplinary action up to and including dismissal or termination of contract. Retaliation against anyone who reports bullying or participates in an investigation will not be tolerated.
Communication and review

This policy is communicated to all workers and reviewed annually. Implementing it creates a safe and respectful workplace, supports morale and productivity, and protects the Company from legal liability.
Statement

The Modern Slavery Act 2015 requires certain businesses to disclose the steps they take to address slavery and human trafficking in their supply chains. Although the Company may fall below the statutory turnover threshold, it makes this statement voluntarily as a matter of good practice. Throughout this statement, 'slavery and human trafficking' encompasses all forms of coerced labour.

The Company is committed to maintaining and improving systems and processes to avoid complicity in human rights violations in its own operations and its supply chain. The Company does not tolerate forced, bonded (including debt bondage) or indentured labour, involuntary prison labour, slavery or trafficking of persons, or harsh or inhumane treatment, and expects the same of its suppliers and subcontractors.
Steps taken
Clear expectations are set for suppliers and subcontractors through the Company's supplier approval process and terms of engagement, and suppliers are regularly reminded of their obligation to comply

Right to work checks are carried out for all workers in accordance with the Right to Work & Migrant Workers Policy, and workers are paid at or above the applicable statutory minimum through auditable payroll

Recruitment is carried out directly or through reputable agencies; the Company remains alert to warning signs such as workers sharing bank accounts or addresses, withheld identity documents, or third parties controlling wages
The Directors set the tone of the Company's ethical culture and communicate the importance of ethics and legal compliance to all staff

Anyone, employees, subcontractors, suppliers or clients, is encouraged to report in good faith any concerns about slavery, human trafficking or other ethical, human rights, legal or regulatory violations, and may do so under the Whistleblowing Policy
Review
This statement is reviewed and reissued annually.

policies.title: Right to Work & Migrant Workers Policy

runs.t: Policy statement

The Company supports the fair employment of migrant workers and the prevention of illegal working, in line with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 and current Home Office guidance for employers. This policy applies to all employees and workers engaged by the Company, including agency workers. Employing someone without the right to do the work in question can result in civil penalties of up to £45,000 per worker for a first breach and up to £60,000 per worker for repeat breaches, and criminal liability where illegal working is knowing or reasonably suspected.
Right to work checks
Before any person commences work, the Company will carry out a right to work check using one of the Home Office approved methods:
An online right to work check via the Home Office service, using a share code provided by the individual, for those with digital immigration status (eVisa) or a biometric residence permit or card
A manual check of original acceptable documents (for example a British or Irish passport) in the presence of the holder, with a clear, dated copy retained
A check via a certified Identity Service Provider using identity document validation technology, where applicable, for British and Irish citizens with valid passports

Checks are carried out on all prospective workers regardless of nationality, ethnicity or accent, to ensure the process is non-discriminatory. Where a worker has a time-limited right to work, a follow-up check is diarised and completed before permission expires. Evidence of every check is retained securely for the duration of employment and for two years after it ends.
Health, safety and fair treatment of migrant workers
Ensure workers have the knowledge, skills and competence to do their work safely, and verify that overseas vocational qualifications are compatible with GB requirements
Carry out risk assessments of the tasks workers will undertake and ensure control measures are in place, maintained and communicated
Provide induction and job-related training, and information on risks and precautions, in a form workers can understand
Consider the needs of workers who may not speak English well, including translation of key safety information and use of visual materials where appropriate
Ensure workers are adequately supervised and can communicate with their supervisors
Review
This policy is reviewed annually and in line with changes to Home Office guidance and immigration legislation.

policies.title: Data Protection & Information Security Policy (UK GDPR)

runs.t: Policy statement

The Company collects and processes personal data in the course of its business and is committed to handling it lawfully, fairly and securely in accordance with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018. The Company is registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) as a data controller and pays the applicable data protection fee.
Data protection principles

The Company ensures that personal data is: processed lawfully, fairly and transparently; collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary; accurate and kept up to date; kept for no longer than necessary; and processed securely. The Company is responsible for, and able to demonstrate, compliance with these principles (accountability).
Personal data we process

The Company processes personal data relating to employees and workers (including recruitment records, right to work documentation, payroll and bank details, training and competency records, health surveillance and occupational health information, and accident records), clients and their representatives, suppliers and subcontractors, and site personnel (including sign-in and induction records). Special category data, such as health information, is processed only where a lawful condition applies, for example to comply with employment and health and safety obligations.
Lawful bases

Personal data is processed only where a lawful basis applies: performance of a contract, compliance with a legal obligation (including health and safety, right to work and tax legislation), legitimate interests, consent, or protection of vital interests. Where consent is relied upon it may be withdrawn at any time.
Individual rights

Individuals have rights over their personal data, including the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, and the right to object. The Company will respond to a valid request within one calendar month. Identity may be verified before a request is actioned; there is no fee for a standard request.
Data sharing, processors and international transfers

Personal data is not sold and is only shared where necessary for the purposes described, or where required by law. Third-party processors (for example payroll, IT, accreditation and document platforms) act only on the Company's instructions under contracts containing the safeguards required by the UK GDPR. Personal data is not transferred outside the United Kingdom unless an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguard (such as the International Data Transfer Agreement) is in place.
Security and retention

The Company applies appropriate technical and organisational measures, including access controls and password protection, secure storage of paper records, secure platforms for transmitting sensitive information, and secure destruction at the end of retention periods. Personal data is retained only as long as necessary for its purpose or as required by law, and records are reviewed periodically.
Responsibilities for sensitive material and data
{{signer}}, {{role}}, has overall responsibility for the security of sensitive material and data held by the Company, approves who has access to it, and makes sure these arrangements are followed

Office and management staff are responsible for the records they handle, including personnel, payroll, client, tender and commercial information, and for keeping them in the Company's approved systems only

Supervisors are responsible for sensitive material held on site, including drawings, client documents, sign-in and induction records and health information, and for making sure it is not left unattended or on display

Every worker is responsible for protecting the information and devices issued to them, for using them only for Company business, and for reporting any loss, theft or suspected breach to a Director immediately
Subcontractors, suppliers and other third parties who are given sensitive information are required to protect it to the same standard and to use it only for the purpose for which it was provided
IT and data security arrangements
Firewalls: the firewall on the office and home routers and the firewall built into each computer are kept switched on, and default router passwords are changed
Virus scanning: anti-virus and anti-malware software is installed on all computers and laptops, updates itself automatically and scans files and downloads as they are opened

Password protection: all laptops, computers, tablets and mobile phones used for Company business are protected by a password, PIN or biometric lock and lock automatically when left idle; laptops and mobile devices are encrypted

Accounts: each user has their own login, passwords are strong and not shared or reused, and multi-factor authentication is switched on for email, cloud storage, banking and accounts systems wherever it is available
Updates: operating systems, applications and apps are kept supported and are updated automatically
Access: access to sensitive information is limited to those who need it for their work and is removed on the day a person leaves the Company
Transmission and removable media: sensitive information is sent by secure platform or password-protected file, and is not held on USB sticks or personal accounts
Paper records are kept in locked storage and are shredded at the end of their retention period; devices are securely wiped before disposal or reissue
How and where information is stored

The Company's information is held electronically in established business cloud platforms, including its email, document storage, accounts, payroll and compliance systems, and in standard office software files saved to those platforms, with a limited amount of paper records kept in locked storage. The Company does not operate its own servers. Any equipment holding Company data that is kept at its premises is in a locked building with access limited to authorised staff. The Company's cloud providers hold data in data centres in the United Kingdom, or in countries covered by UK adequacy regulations or the appropriate safeguards described above.
Confidentiality and conflicts of interest

Confidentiality clauses are standard in the Company's contracts of employment and in its orders and agreements with subcontractors and suppliers, and they continue to apply after the contract ends. Information belonging to one client, including drawings, prices, programmes and tender information, is kept separately from that of other clients, is accessible only to those working on that client's project, and is never disclosed to or used for the benefit of another client. Any person who has a personal or business interest that could conflict with the handling of a client's information declares it to a Director, who decides whether that person is to be kept away from the information concerned.
Personal data breaches

Any actual or suspected personal data breach must be reported to a Director immediately. The Company will assess and contain the breach and, where it is likely to result in a risk to individuals, notify the ICO without undue delay and within 72 hours of becoming aware. Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, those affected will also be informed. All breaches are recorded, whether or not notifiable.
Responsibilities, training and review

The Directors act as the Company's data protection lead. All members of the workforce who handle personal or sensitive data receive data protection and information security training at induction, covering this policy, the secure handling of information, recognising phishing and other scams, and how to report a breach. Refresher training is given at least annually, by briefing or toolbox talk, and whenever the arrangements change, and a record of the training is kept. Complaints may be raised with the Company or with the ICO (ico.org.uk). This policy is reviewed annually and in line with changes to legislation or ICO guidance.
Policy statement

{{company}} depends on its computers, mobile devices, email and online systems to run its business and to look after information belonging to its clients, workforce and supply chain. The Company is committed to protecting those systems and that information against cyber attack, loss and misuse, using security controls that are proportionate to the size of the business and to the data it holds. The Company follows the guidance for small businesses published by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC). This policy has been approved by {{signer}}, {{role}}, who has overall responsibility for cyber security. It applies to everyone who uses the Company's systems or data, and it is read alongside the Data Protection & Information Security Policy.
Identifying data and systems

The Company keeps a register of the information and systems it manages. The register lists each device, account and online platform used for Company business, the information held on it, who has access, and who is responsible for it. Each entry is graded by how sensitive the information is and how much the business relies on the system, so that the strongest controls are applied where the loss would do the most harm, for example to banking, payroll, personnel records and client information. The register is reviewed by a Director at least annually and whenever a device, system or supplier is added or removed.
Security controls
Firewalls and routers: firewalls are switched on for the office and home internet connections and on each computer, and default passwords on routers and other equipment are changed
Secure set-up: devices are set up with only the software and accounts that are needed; unused software and accounts are removed

Access control: each user has their own account with only the access their work requires; administrator accounts are used only for administration; multi-factor authentication is used for email, cloud storage, banking and accounts systems wherever it is available; access is removed when a person leaves

Malware protection: anti-virus and anti-malware software is active on all computers and laptops and updates automatically; software and apps are installed only from the manufacturer's or official app stores
Updates: operating systems and software are kept in support and security updates are installed promptly, automatically wherever possible
Devices: laptops, tablets and phones are locked by password, PIN or biometric, are encrypted, and are able to be located and wiped remotely where the device supports it
Email and payments: staff are trained to recognise phishing; any request to change bank details or make an unexpected payment is verified by telephone, using a known number, before it is acted on
Suppliers: IT and online service providers are chosen with regard to their security arrangements, and the security settings they provide are switched on
Logging and monitoring

The Company uses the logging built into its systems. Its email, cloud storage, banking and accounts platforms record sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts, changes to accounts and permissions and access to files, and its computers and security software record security events and detected threats. Security alerts from these systems are sent to a Director and are acted on when received. The logs are reviewed by a Director periodically, and immediately following any alert or suspected incident, and are kept for at least as long as each system allows as standard.
Backups of critical systems

The Company's critical systems and data, including email, project and client documents, accounts and payroll records, and compliance records, are backed up automatically at least daily to a secure cloud location that is separate from the device or system being backed up. Access to the backups is restricted. A test restore is carried out at least annually to confirm that information can be recovered.
Incident response

A cyber security incident includes a lost or stolen device, a suspected virus or ransomware infection, a compromised password or account, a successful phishing or payment fraud attempt, and any unauthorised access to Company data. The Company responds as follows:
Report: the person who discovers or suspects an incident reports it to a Director immediately, at any time of day

Contain: the affected device is disconnected from the internet, affected passwords are changed, active sessions are signed out, lost devices are locked or wiped remotely, and the bank is contacted at once where money or bank details are involved
Assess: the Director establishes what happened, which systems and data are affected and whether personal or client data is involved, using the system logs
Recover: devices are cleaned or rebuilt and data is restored from backup, with outside IT support brought in where needed; systems are returned to use only when they are confirmed to be secure

Notify: where personal data is at risk the Information Commissioner's Office is notified within 72 hours and those affected are informed, as set out in the Data Protection & Information Security Policy; affected clients are told promptly; fraud and cyber crime are reported to Action Fraud, and to the Company's insurer where cover applies
Review: every incident is recorded in the incident log with its cause, the action taken and the lessons learned, and controls and training are improved as a result
Home and remote working

Members of the workforce work from home, from site and while travelling. The Company has assessed the threats this creates. The main threats are: home or public Wi-Fi that is not secure; devices shared with or seen by family members and others; loss or theft of devices and papers in transit, in vehicles or on site; screens and telephone calls being overlooked or overheard; and phishing or impersonation attempts being harder to check when working alone. The assessment is reviewed annually with this policy. The following guidance applies to all home and remote working:
Use only devices that meet the security controls in this policy; Company information is not saved to personal devices or personal accounts
Protect the home Wi-Fi with a strong password and change the router's default password; do not use public Wi-Fi for Company business unless through a mobile hotspot or secure connection
Lock the screen whenever the device is left, and do not allow family members or others to use a device that holds Company information
Keep devices and papers out of sight and never leave them in an unattended vehicle; store them securely at home
Take care that screens and conversations cannot be seen or overheard in public places
Check any unusual or urgent request by telephone with a colleague before acting on it
Return or securely destroy paper records, and report any loss or concern to a Director immediately
Training and awareness

Everyone who uses the Company's systems is briefed on this policy at induction and receives cyber security awareness training at least annually, covering passwords, phishing, safe use of devices, home working and how to report an incident. Records of the training are kept.
Approval and review

This policy is approved by {{signer}}, {{role}}, on behalf of {{company}}. It is reviewed at least every 12 months, and sooner following a security incident, a change to the Company's systems or a change in NCSC guidance, and it is reissued with the date of each review.
Policy statement

{{company}} is committed to delivering work of consistently high quality that meets client requirements, complies with all relevant legislation, standards and specifications, and is delivered right first time. The Company operates a documented quality management system aligned with the principles of ISO 9001, customer focus, leadership, engagement of people, a process approach, evidence-based decision making, improvement, and relationship management, proportionate to the size and nature of the business.
Responsibility:

{{signer}}, {{role}}, has overall responsibility for quality and for the implementation of these arrangements. Supervisors are responsible for the quality of work under their control on a day-to-day basis, and every worker is responsible for the quality of their own work and for reporting defects and non-conformances.
Quality objectives and performance indicators
The Company sets measurable quality objectives, reviewed at the annual management review. Current objectives include:
Zero defects outstanding at handover, with any snagging items closed out within agreed timescales
Completion of projects on or ahead of the agreed programme
Acknowledgement of client complaints within 2 working days and a substantive response within 10 working days
No repeat non-conformances of the same root cause within 12 months
Maintenance of approved-supplier performance, with any supplier issues resolved through documented corrective action
Performance against these indicators is tracked through inspection records, the complaints log, the non-conformance register and supplier reviews.
Document and record control
Current versions of drawings, specifications, RAMS, procedures and policies are issued to those who need them; superseded documents are withdrawn from use and marked or archived
A version control log records the history, changes and approval of controlled documents, including this policy pack

Quality records, inspections, test results, certificates, delivery records, training records, complaints and corrective actions, are retained securely and are retrievable for client and assessor review
Project delivery controls

Pre-start review: before work commences, each project is reviewed to confirm client requirements, the specification, applicable standards and building regulations, inspection and test requirements, and any hold or witness points required by the client
Setting out and verification: dimensions, levels and interfaces are checked against the drawings before and during the works

Stage inspections: work is inspected at defined stages by a supervisor or other competent person, including before work is covered up; where the project warrants it, an inspection and test plan (ITP) is prepared and records kept against each stage

Snagging and handover: a pre-handover inspection identifies and closes out defects; completed works are inspected with the client where practicable, and certificates, warranties, product information and operation and maintenance details are provided in the handover pack
Product classification, selection and conformity
The Company recognises its duties in relation to the classification and conformity of construction products, including under the Construction Products Regulations and the Building Safety Act 2022:
Products are classified and selected according to their intended use, the project specification, and the relevant designated or harmonised standard applicable to that product type

Where a product is covered by a designated or harmonised standard, only products bearing the required UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA), UK(NI) or CE marking and accompanied by a Declaration of Performance (or Declaration of Conformity, as applicable) are used; a product without the appropriate marking is not used in the works
Products are procured only from reputable manufacturers and merchants to guard against counterfeit, substituted or non-conforming products; certificates and declarations are obtained and retained
Hazardous substances are classified, labelled and controlled in accordance with the CLP Regulation and COSHH; safety data sheets are obtained and COSHH assessments completed before use

Traceability is maintained through retention of delivery records, batch or serial numbers where applicable, Declarations of Performance, certificates and warranties, passed to the client in handover documentation where required
Non-conforming, damaged or suspect products are quarantined, clearly marked and not incorporated into the works; the supplier is notified and the non-conformance recorded
Product substitutions are not made without approval and verification that the substitute meets the specification and conformity requirements
Checking conformity marking and documentation
The Company checks for the presence of the UKCA, UK(NI) or CE marking and the other necessary documents at three points:

Before ordering: the person placing the order confirms from the manufacturer's or merchant's product information that the product carries the marking required for its intended use and that a Declaration of Performance or Declaration of Conformity is available for it

On delivery: the supervisor or other person receiving the goods checks the product, its label and packaging and the delivery documents against the order and the specification, confirms that the marking is present, and confirms that the declaration and any test certificates, third-party certification, safety data sheets and manufacturer's installation instructions are held; the check is recorded on the delivery note or goods received record
Before installation: the supervisor confirms that the product about to be installed is the product that was specified and checked, and that it is undamaged and within any stated shelf life

A product that arrives without the required marking or documents is not accepted for use; it is quarantined and handled as a non-conforming product until the supplier provides the documents or replaces it
Declarations, certificates and delivery records are kept on the project file and are available to the client and to assessors
Products from suppliers outside the United Kingdom

Wherever possible the Company buys construction products through UK manufacturers and merchants. Where a product is bought directly from a supplier outside the United Kingdom, the Company recognises that it may take on the duties of an importer, and before the order is placed {{signer}} or a person nominated by them checks that the supplier has taken the necessary steps:
The manufacturer has had the product's performance assessed against the relevant designated or harmonised standard, using an approved or notified body where the standard requires one
The manufacturer has drawn up the Declaration of Performance or Declaration of Conformity and the supporting technical documentation, and the product carries the UKCA, UK(NI) or CE marking
Copies of the declaration, test reports and certificates are obtained and kept, together with instructions and safety information in English
The manufacturer's name and address, and the importer's name and address where required, are shown on the product, its packaging or the accompanying documents, so that the product can be traced
Where this documentation cannot be obtained, the product is not purchased
Inspection and approval of installed products and systems
The installation of construction products and systems is checked and approved by a competent person before the work is covered up, handed over or put into use.

Competent person: the supervisor, or another person appointed by {{signer}}, who holds the trade qualification, training and experience relevant to the product or system being installed; for specialist systems, the person holds the qualification, registration or manufacturer's approval that the system requires

What is checked: that the product installed is the product specified, and that it has been installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, the drawings and specification, the relevant standards and the performance declared for the product

Inspection and test plan: for each stage of the work the plan sets out what is inspected or tested, the acceptance criteria, who carries out the check and who approves it, any hold or witness points required by the client, and the record to be kept

Benchmarking: for repeated elements of work, the first completed example is inspected by the competent person, and agreed with the client where required, and is then the benchmark standard against which the remaining work is checked

Approval: the competent person signs and dates the inspection record, supported by photographs where work is to be covered up; work that does not pass is not approved, is corrected and reinspected, and is entered on the non-conformance register
Testing and commissioning results and certificates are completed by the competent person and included in the handover pack
Non-conformance and corrective action

Non-conforming work or materials are recorded on the non-conformance register, with the immediate correction, the root cause, and the corrective action taken to prevent recurrence. Corrective actions are assigned an owner and a completion date, and their effectiveness is verified before close-out. The register is reviewed periodically for trends, which feed into training and procedural improvements.
Client feedback and complaints

Feedback is sought from clients on completion of works. Complaints are logged on receipt, acknowledged within 2 working days, investigated impartially, and responded to substantively within 10 working days, with the outcome and any corrective action recorded. Lessons learned are communicated to relevant staff and fed back into procedures.
Supply chain quality

Suppliers and subcontractors are selected and evaluated using the Company's approval process, which considers quality arrangements, competence, insurances and accreditations. Quality requirements, including applicable standards and specifications, are communicated in orders and contracts. Performance is monitored, non-conformance is managed through documented corrective action, and periodic reviews or audits of key suppliers may be undertaken.
Competence and training

Quality-related training needs are identified from the types of work undertaken and the requirements of specifications and standards. Training is delivered through induction, on-the-job instruction and toolbox talks, including workmanship standards and product conformity, and its effectiveness is evaluated through inspection results and supervision. Training and competency records (including cards and qualifications) are retained.
Monitoring, audit and management review

Compliance with these arrangements is monitored through site inspections and periodic internal audits of projects and records. The Directors carry out a management review at least annually, considering performance against quality objectives, inspection and audit findings, non-conformances, complaints, client feedback and supplier performance, and set improvement actions with owners and dates. This policy is reviewed at the management review and following significant non-conformances or changes to legislation and standards.
Policy statement

{{company}} recognises its duties under the Building Safety Act 2022 and under Part 2A of the Building Regulations 2010 (dutyholders and competence), which apply to all building work and not only to higher-risk buildings, together with the equivalent requirements in Wales. The Company acts as a contractor under these Regulations. It is committed to making sure that the building work it carries out complies with all relevant requirements of the Building Regulations, that the people who carry it out are competent, and that nothing it does compromises the structural safety or fire safety of a building. These duties are separate from, and additional to, the Company's duties under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015.

{{signer}}, {{role}}, has overall responsibility for this policy and for making sure the Company has the organisational capability, meaning the management arrangements, resources, procedures and supervision, to meet its duties. Supervisors are responsible for applying these arrangements on site. Every worker is responsible for working within their competence and for reporting anything that could affect compliance or the safety of a building.
Higher-risk buildings

A higher-risk building, during design and construction, is a building that is at least 18 metres in height or has at least 7 storeys and that contains at least two residential units, or is a hospital or care home of that height. Before accepting work, the Company establishes from the client or principal contractor whether the building is a higher-risk building. Where it is, the additional arrangements in this policy apply, including the golden thread of information, change control and mandatory occurrence reporting, and the Company works to the building control approval given by the Building Safety Regulator.
Competence management

The Company only accepts and carries out work that it is competent to do, and it does not allow any person to carry out work that is beyond their competence. Competence is assessed against four elements for each job role: skills, knowledge, experience and behaviours. The Company's arrangements have regard to BS 8670-1:2024, the core criteria for building safety in competence frameworks.

Role requirements: for each role (Director, supervisor, tradesperson, apprentice or trainee, labourer) the Company records the qualifications, cards, training, experience and behaviours required, including knowledge of the parts of the Building Regulations relevant to the work

Pre-qualification and onboarding: before a person starts, their qualifications, cards and experience are checked and verified, references are taken where appropriate, and they are inducted in this policy and the Quality Policy

Assessment: competence, including behaviour (following the specification and manufacturer's instructions, not covering up defects, speaking up, and refusing work they are not competent to do), is assessed when a person starts and then periodically through supervision, inspection of their work and an annual review linked to training needs

Records: a training and competence matrix is kept for the whole workforce, showing qualifications, cards and training, with expiry dates tracked and renewals arranged before they fall due; certificates, inductions, toolbox talks and continuing professional development are recorded and retrievable

Training: the workforce receives training on the Building Safety Act and the Building Regulations relevant to their work, including fire safety and fire-stopping awareness, structural safety, product conformity and the reporting arrangements in this policy
Trainees: a person who is still developing their competence works only under the close supervision of a competent person, who checks and takes responsibility for their work

Competence failures: where work or behaviour shows that a person is not competent for a task, they are taken off that task, the work is checked and corrected, the matter is recorded as a non-conformance, and retraining and closer supervision are put in place before they return to it

Ceasing to be competent: where the Company finds that it no longer meets the competence requirements for work it has taken on, it tells the principal contractor or the person who appointed it without delay
Subcontractors and the supply chain

Before appointing a subcontractor or labour-only worker, the Company takes reasonable steps to satisfy itself that they have the skills, knowledge, experience and behaviours, and where they are an organisation the organisational capability, for the work. This is done through a pre-qualification questionnaire and checks of qualifications, cards, accreditations, references and previous work. Subcontractors are asked specifically to confirm and evidence their current competence for any work that affects fire safety or structural safety, such as fire-stopping, fire doors, compartment walls and floors, cavity barriers and structural elements. For work on a higher-risk building, they are also asked to declare any serious sanction or relevant misconduct in the previous five years. Competence obligations are written into subcontract orders. Subcontractors are inducted, briefed, supervised and inspected in the same way as the Company's own workforce, their work is checked and signed off, and any shortfall is dealt with through documented corrective action.
Supervision, instruction and information

Supervisors: plan the work, brief the method, the drawings and specification and the relevant Building Regulations requirements, check competence before allocating tasks, inspect the work and sign it off
Workers: follow the briefed method, the specification and the manufacturer's instructions, work only within their competence, and stop and ask where information is missing or unclear
Subcontractors: supervise their own workforce to the same standard and work under the overall supervision of the Company's supervisor

Methods of supervision: site induction, briefing of RAMS, toolbox talks, competence checks, inspection at each stage and before work is covered up, permits to work where required, and signed inspection records

Changes to legislation, standards or the project requirements are briefed to those affected before the change takes effect; breaches of these arrangements are dealt with through the non-conformance and disciplinary procedures
Records of inductions, briefings, inspections and sign-offs are kept securely and are available to clients and assessors
Client awareness of duties

The Company does not start building work unless it is satisfied that the client is aware of the duties placed on clients by the Building Regulations. Where the Company is appointed directly by a client, including a domestic client, it explains those duties in writing before work starts, using its standard client duties letter, and keeps a copy with the client's acknowledgement. Where the Company is appointed by a principal contractor or another contractor, it obtains confirmation from them before starting that the client has been made aware of its duties.
Planning, managing and monitoring building work

Planning: before work starts the Company reviews the drawings and specification, identifies the elements of its work that affect fire safety and structural safety, confirms that the design information is sufficient to build in compliance with the Building Regulations, raises any concern about the design with the principal contractor or designer, and agrees roles, sequence and interfaces with other trades

Managing: only competent people are allocated to the work; only products that are specified and that carry the required conformity marking and documentation are used, as set out in the Quality Policy; no product is substituted and no detail is changed without approval; the supply chain is checked; and site emergency and fire arrangements are followed

Monitoring: work is supervised and inspected at each stage and before it is covered up, with photographs kept; it is checked and approved by a competent person; defects are recorded, corrected and reinspected; and inspection records are audited periodically by a Director

Completion: on handover the Company provides the information required for the building's records, including product information, Declarations of Performance, certificates, test results, as-built information and inspection records, and where it finishes its work on a higher-risk building before the project is complete it reports to the principal contractor on the matters the Regulations require
Learning: near misses, defects and lessons learned are reviewed, shared with the workforce in briefings and toolbox talks, and used to improve procedures and training
Cooperation, communication and providing information

The Company cooperates with the client, the principal designer, designers, the principal contractor and other contractors so that the building work complies with all relevant requirements, and it complies with the directions of the principal contractor. It provides information to, and receives information from, those dutyholders as follows:
A named point of contact, the supervisor or {{signer}}, is given to the principal contractor for each project
The Company attends pre-start, coordination and progress meetings, site inductions and briefings, and keeps a note of decisions and actions

RAMS, product and technical information, programmes, progress updates and inspection records are provided in writing, and the Company takes account of other work that affects or is affected by its own
Risks to compliance, delays, design queries and proposed changes are reported to the principal contractor immediately and confirmed in writing

Information is exchanged through the document management system or Common Data Environment named by the client or principal contractor for the project; where none is named, the Company's own secure cloud document storage is used, with documents indexed by project and version controlled
A record is kept of what information was shared, with whom and when, and of the action that followed
Disagreements or unresolved concerns are escalated to {{signer}}, who raises them with the principal contractor's management
Golden thread of information

For work on a higher-risk building, the Company contributes to the golden thread of information kept by the client and principal contractor. {{signer}} is responsible for this. Information about the Company's work is collected as the work proceeds (products installed and their locations, Declarations of Performance and certificates, installation and inspection records, photographs, test results and as-built details), is stored electronically, indexed by project, location and date, kept accurate and up to date with version control, and uploaded to the project's named Common Data Environment or supplied to the principal contractor in the digital format they require and at the intervals they require. The information supplied is checked for completeness by a Director before it is issued and at handover.
Change control

The Company does not depart from the approved design, specification or products without the change being authorised through the project's change control procedure. For work on a higher-risk building, the Company gives the client and principal contractor the information they need to update the change control log before any change is made: a description of the proposed change; the reason for it; whether the Company considers it a recordable, notifiable or major change; the name and occupation of anyone consulted and a summary of their advice; the documents affected, with revised versions; and an explanation of how the work will continue to comply with the Building Regulations after the change. The change is not carried out until written approval is received, and the Company keeps a digital record of each request and approval.
Reporting non-compliance and safety occurrences

Any person working for the Company who sees or suspects something that could mean building work does not comply with the Building Regulations, or that could affect the structural safety or fire safety of a building, reports it immediately to their supervisor. This applies to the Company's own work and to the work of others, and it includes defective work, incomplete or damaged compartmentation and fire-stopping, missing cavity barriers, incorrect or substituted products, inadequate fire precautions and damage to structural elements.

The supervisor stops the affected work where necessary, records the matter with photographs on the Company's non-compliance log, and reports it to the principal contractor the same day, confirmed in writing

On a higher-risk building, a matter that could present a risk of death or serious injury to a significant number of people through structural failure or the spread of fire is a safety occurrence, and it is reported at once through the principal contractor's mandatory occurrence reporting system

{{signer}} follows up each report until it is resolved; where a serious concern is not acted on, it is escalated to the principal contractor's senior management, to the client and, if it remains unresolved, to the building control authority or the Building Safety Regulator
The workforce is trained at induction and by toolbox talk to recognise these breaches and in how to report them

Reports can be made in confidence under the Company's Whistleblowing Policy, which applies to these building safety concerns, and no person will suffer any detriment for raising a concern in good faith
Scheduled inspections, the non-compliance log and coordination meetings are used to check that reported matters have been closed out
Keeping up to date

The Company keeps up to date with changes to the Building Safety Act, the Building Regulations and Approved Documents, other legislation and relevant standards through its retained adviser, Safety Simplified Ltd, through updates from the Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK, through Build UK and its trade and accreditation bodies, and through the technical information issued by manufacturers and principal contractors. {{signer}} reviews these updates, amends procedures where needed, and briefs the workforce on any change that affects their work by briefing or toolbox talk, with further training arranged where required. Briefings are recorded.
Review
This policy is reviewed at least annually at the management review, and sooner following a change in legislation or guidance, a reported safety occurrence, or a significant non-compliance.
Purpose and scope

The purpose of this policy is to ensure that the risks associated with the Company's business activities are effectively identified, assessed and controlled, and that risk management is integrated into all aspects of the business. It applies to all employees, contractors and stakeholders involved in the Company's activities.
Risk management process
Risk identification: all potential risks associated with business activities are identified, including those arising from equipment, materials, tools, work activities and the working environment
Risk assessment: the likelihood and severity of each identified risk is assessed, taking into account the consequences should the risk materialise

Risk control: measures are implemented to control and mitigate identified risks; risk assessments and method statements (RAMS) must be read, understood and signed by all relevant parties before work commences
Monitoring and review: the effectiveness of control measures is continuously monitored and reviewed, and adjusted as necessary
Responsibilities and review

All employees and contractors have a responsibility to identify and report potential risks to management. Management is responsible for ensuring the risk management process operates, that workers are trained in its implementation, and that RAMS are signed before work commences. This policy and the supporting processes are reviewed continuously, considering feedback from workers and stakeholders and changes in legislation and industry best practice.
Policy statement

{{company}} is committed to protecting the environment, preventing pollution, complying with all applicable environmental legislation, and continually improving its environmental performance. The Company operates environmental management arrangements aligned with the principles of ISO 14001, plan, do, check, act, proportionate to the size and nature of the business. Environmental management is a responsibility of management and supervision and depends on the co-operation of every employee, whose duty it is to comply with this policy and act responsibly at all times.
Responsibility:

{{signer}}, {{role}}, is the designated person with overall responsibility for environmental management and compliance, including maintaining these arrangements, monitoring performance, and reporting environmental matters at management review. Supervisors implement the arrangements on site day to day.
Environmental aspects and impacts

The Company identifies the environmental aspects of its activities and assesses their impacts and significance, maintaining a register that is reviewed annually and when new types of work are undertaken. Significant aspects for the business include:
Generation of construction waste, packaging waste and offcuts
Use of raw materials, energy, fuel and water
Storage and use of fuels, oils, adhesives, paints and other chemicals
Emissions to air from vehicles and plant, and dust from work activities
Potential discharges or run-off to drains and watercourses
Noise and vibration affecting neighbours and site personnel
Transport and vehicle movements
Legal compliance

The Company maintains awareness of the environmental legislation applicable to its activities and evaluates its compliance as part of monitoring and management review. Key legislation includes: the Environmental Protection Act 1990 (including the section 34 duty of care for waste); the Environment Act 2021; the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011; the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005; the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016; the Water Resources Act 1991; the Control of Pollution Act 1974; the Clean Air Act 1993; the Noise and Statutory Nuisance Act 1993; the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981; and the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002. Legislative updates are monitored and reflected in these arrangements.
Objectives and targets
The Company sets measurable environmental objectives, reviewed at the annual management review. Current objectives include:
Zero pollution incidents and zero enforcement action
Segregation of waste streams on all projects where space permits, and disposal only through registered carriers to licensed or permitted facilities, targeting maximum diversion of waste from landfill
100% of waste transfers documented with transfer or consignment notes, retained for the statutory periods
Reduction of fuel and energy use through vehicle maintenance, route planning and a no-idling expectation for plant and vehicles
Preference for recycled, recyclable and responsibly sourced materials (for example FSC or PEFC certified timber) where the specification allows
Waste management

The Company complies with its duty of care under the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, applying the waste hierarchy: prevent, reuse, recycle, recover, dispose. Waste is stored correctly and segregated where practicable; transfers are documented with waste transfer notes (or consignment notes for hazardous waste) and carried out only by registered waste carriers to licensed or permitted facilities, whose registrations are checked. Transfer notes are retained for two years and hazardous waste consignment notes for three years. Fly-tipping is prohibited, whether directly or through third parties, and burning of waste is prohibited. Hazardous wastes (for example asbestos-containing materials, solvents, contaminated packaging and used absorbents) are identified, stored separately and consigned in accordance with the Hazardous Waste Regulations 2005.
Pollution prevention and operational controls
Fuel and chemical storage: fuels, oils and chemicals are stored in bunded containers or on drip trays, away from drains and watercourses, with containers returned to storage after use

Spill response: spill kits are available where fuels and chemicals are used; spillages are contained and cleaned up immediately, contaminated absorbents are disposed of as hazardous waste, and all spills are reported and recorded

Water protection: discharges to drains or watercourses are prevented; wastewater and washout arising from works is collected and disposed of appropriately, in compliance with the Water Resources Act 1991 and the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016

Nuisance: noise, dust, vibration, odour and smoke are minimised by best practicable means, including plant selection and maintenance, damping down, sheeting of loads, and consideration of working hours and neighbours
Air quality: vehicles and plant are maintained to minimise emissions and engines are switched off when not in use

Ecology and heritage: where work is near habitats of protected species, appropriate protective measures are taken in line with wildlife legislation; if archaeological remains or suspected contaminated land are discovered, work in the affected area proceeds with due care and the client is notified promptly Housekeeping: sites are kept clean and tidy, rubbish is removed at frequent intervals, and materials are stored safely and securely so they do not present a hazard or a pollution risk
Emergency preparedness and incident reporting

For activities with a credible risk of a significant environmental incident, contingency measures are planned before work starts, including containment equipment and clear responsibility for response. Environmental incidents and near misses are reported to management immediately, contained, investigated and recorded, and any notification required to a regulator or client is made promptly, within 24 hours to the client in the case of an incident or non-compliance on their premises. Remedial action is taken to make good any environmental damage.
Monitoring, audit and management review

Site inspections include environmental checks (waste storage and segregation, fuel and chemical storage, spill kit availability, nuisance controls and housekeeping). Periodic internal audits verify that these arrangements are being followed and that records, transfer notes, carrier registrations, inspection records, incident reports, are complete. The Directors review environmental performance at least annually, considering performance against objectives, incidents and near misses, complaints, audit findings and legislative changes, and set improvement actions. Records of audits, incidents and non-compliances are retained for six years.
Supply chain

Suppliers and subcontractors whose activities have significant environmental impacts are evaluated through the Company's approval process, which considers their environmental procedures, waste carrier registrations, permits and compliance history. Environmental requirements are communicated in orders and contracts, evidence such as tip tickets and carrier registrations is obtained and checked, and non-conformance is managed through documented corrective action.
Training and communication

Environmental responsibilities are communicated to all employees at induction and reinforced through toolbox talks (including waste segregation and spill response), team meetings and written information. Training records are retained. This policy is displayed and available at each office and workplace, and is available to interested parties on request.
Complaints

Environmental complaints are logged on receipt with the complainant's details and the nature of the concern, acknowledged promptly, investigated, and assessed against legal requirements and these arrangements. Where a complaint is upheld, corrective action is taken with realistic timescales communicated to the complainant, monitored to completion and recorded. Complaints are reviewed periodically for recurring issues, and lessons learned are incorporated into these arrangements.
Energy and carbon

The Company monitors its fuel and energy use through fuel records and utility billing, and reduces its carbon impact through vehicle maintenance and efficient route planning, a no-idling expectation, procurement of energy-efficient plant and equipment at replacement, and reduction and recycling of waste. Opportunities to reduce emissions are considered at management review.
Policy statement

The Company understands the need to be a good corporate citizen and believes that sustainability, meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own, and corporate responsibility are closely linked. The Company recognises its obligations to all its stakeholders (clients, employees, suppliers and wider society), engages with them openly and honestly, and promotes responsible business practice throughout the business. This policy is applied in four areas: marketplace, workplace, environment and community.
Marketplace

The Company's mission is to understand its clients' needs and deliver services of good value, consistent quality, reliability and safety. The Company promotes itself ethically, develops secure long-term relationships with suppliers and subcontractors based on mutual trust, pays them on time and to agreed terms, and does not use its purchasing power unscrupulously.
Workplace

Employees are the Company's most important asset. The Company seeks to recruit and retain good people reflecting the diversity of the communities in which it operates, gives equal opportunities to all staff, and provides training and development for fulfilling careers, supported by its Equal Opportunities, Diversity & Inclusion Policy. The health, safety and wellbeing of employees and all those the Company comes into contact with is of paramount importance, managed through the Company's safety management system. Regular two-way communication enables employees to contribute to how the business improves.
Environment

The Company's most significant contribution is through continually improving efficiency on site and in the office, reducing waste, recycling where waste is generated, promoting recycled and sustainably sourced materials, and monitoring energy use and travel to reduce carbon emissions, in accordance with the Environmental Policy.
