Community

The Company is proud that its work enhances the communities in which it operates. It supports local employment of trades and labour and recognises the benefit its activity brings in employment, training, skills and wealth creation. Consideration is given to minimising disruption to neighbours and the public when planning and carrying out works.
Review
The Company sets corporate responsibility objectives, reviews its performance against them, and reviews this policy annually.
Policy statement

The Company is committed to protecting and promoting the mental health and wellbeing of all employees, and to providing a working environment and culture that supports it. This policy complies with health and safety legislation and best practice guidance, including the HSE Management Standards for work-related stress, and is applied in conjunction with related policies including the Drugs & Alcohol Policy and the Equality Act 2010 duty to make reasonable adjustments.
Actions
Reduce stigma and discrimination by increasing awareness and understanding of mental health, and make all staff aware of this policy and the support available
Provide systems that encourage predictable working hours, reasonable workloads and flexible working where appropriate
Ensure all staff have clearly defined roles, objectives and responsibilities, with good management support, appropriate training and adequate resources
Manage conflict effectively and keep the workplace free from bullying, harassment and discrimination
Maintain good two-way communication, particularly during periods of organisational change
Provide training for managers and designated staff in the early identification and appropriate management of mental health issues such as anxiety, depression and stress
Treat individuals experiencing mental health problems fairly, consistently and with non-judgemental, proactive support

Support returns to work, including phased returns, and where a return to the same role is not possible, seek suitable alternatives in consultation with the employee, making reasonable adjustments where required
Treat mental health matters confidentially, sharing information only on a need-to-know basis with the employee's consent
Identify mental health needs within the workforce
Provide opportunities for employees to look after their mental wellbeing, for example through physical activity, stress reducing activities and social events

Ensure a physical environment that is supportive of mental health and wellbeing including a sound, ergonomically designed workstation or working situation with appropriate lighting, noise levels, heating, ventilation and adequate facilities for rest breaks
Signpost employees to support available through the Company, their GP, or external services
Communication and review

All employees are made aware of this policy and the support available, with regular updates provided via management and toolbox talks. Feedback is sought from employees, and this policy is reviewed annually in line with legislative updates and feedback.
Policy statement

Drugs and alcohol affect a person's ability to work safely and can present a danger to themselves and others. The Company expects all workers to be free from the effects of alcohol and drugs (other than prescribed or over-the-counter medication used as directed) during working hours. This policy is designed to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 and, for those who drive, the Road Traffic Act 1988. The Company's approach combines support and enforcement.
Prescribed medication

Where a worker takes prescribed or over-the-counter medication that could affect their ability to work safely, they must inform their supervisor. This will be treated in the strictest confidence and duties adjusted where necessary.
Enforcement
This policy is strictly enforced and disciplinary action will be taken where breaches occur
A worker believed to be unfit through drugs or alcohol will be removed from work and not permitted to return until fit and free from the effects
The Company may conduct random and for-cause drug and alcohol testing; consent will be obtained when testing is conducted, and unreasonable refusal may be treated as a disciplinary matter
Possession of or dealing in illegal drugs on Company premises or sites will be reported to the police
Agency workers, subcontractors or suppliers who breach this policy may have their services terminated
Support

The Company takes a proactive and supportive approach. Workers are encouraged to disclose problems early so support can be arranged, and all disclosures are treated in the strictest confidence, subject to law. Managers are made aware of possible signs of drug or alcohol misuse, such as sudden mood changes, unusual irritability, confusion, fluctuations in concentration or energy, impaired performance, poor timekeeping and deterioration in working relationships. Support may include encouraging the worker to seek help through their GP, time off to attend treatment or support groups, and sick leave, restricted duties or a change of role during treatment where appropriate.

This policy is communicated to all staff on employment and following any updates, and is reviewed annually.
Purpose and scope

The purpose of this policy is to highlight the risks of worker fatigue, the shared responsibility for managing it, and the preventive measures in place, including hours of service limits. It applies to all employees and contractors performing work or activities on behalf of the Company, including those working at offices and sites, those working at remote sites requiring lengthy drives, those who drive as part of their role, and those travelling on Company business. It operates alongside the Working Time Regulations 1998.
Risks of fatigue

Fatigue is an acute or ongoing state of tiredness leading to mental or physical exhaustion that prevents people from functioning safely. Signs include headaches, dizziness, difficulty keeping eyes open, constant yawning and lack of energy. Immediate effects include reduced concentration, short-term memory and reaction times, increased errors, and impaired judgement (including being unaware of the fatigue itself). Fatigue accumulates over time and can be caused by work factors (length of time worked, inadequate rest or sleep, harsh conditions) and lifestyle factors (poor sleep quality, family responsibilities, commuting time).
Responsibilities
Managers and supervisors must take reasonable measures to eliminate or mitigate fatigue risks, plan adequate staffing and realistic schedules, and prevent workers from working excessive hours
Workers must arrive adequately rested, recognise their personal limits, keep track of their hours, and self-report any fatigue concerns before or during work
Fatigue mitigation

Sleep is the only effective long-term strategy for preventing and managing fatigue; adults generally need seven to eight hours of continuous sleep daily, and sleep debt can only be repaid by additional sleep. Rest periods taken through the working day aid recovery, and breaks away from the workstation or vehicle are encouraged, with additional short breaks in harsh conditions such as heat, cold or loud environments.
Working and driving limits
Hours of service, including the commute to and from the work location, must not exceed 14 hours in any 24-hour period
Do not work more than 60 hours in any continuous 7-day period; if exceeded, a minimum of 24 hours away from work is mandatory
Do not drive more than 10 hours within a rolling 24-hour period; take a mandatory 30-minute break after 4.5 hours of driving, and aim for a 15-minute break every 2 hours
Business travel (including personal or rental vehicles, airport commutes and flight time) must not exceed 14 hours in a rolling 24-hour period
Exceeding hours of service

In extraordinary or emergency situations where limits may be exceeded, the worker must discuss this with their supervisor and obtain management approval before continuing. The discussion should cover the effects of continued work and additional risks, and where possible apply mitigation such as mandatory breaks, check-ins on fatigue status, alternative driving arrangements, or sleep accommodation after the work. Any exceedance is documented afterwards.
Purpose

This procedure sets out how the Company communicates its business policies to staff and subcontractors, and how it records evidence that policies have been received, read and understood. These records are retained and made available to clients and accreditation assessors on request.
Distribution arrangements
All new starters receive the current policy pack at induction, and their acknowledgement is recorded before they commence work
When a policy is amended or introduced, the revised pack is issued to all relevant staff and an updated acknowledgement is obtained

Policies are issued digitally and through the Company's acknowledgement register, and are available on request in paper form; key policies are also displayed at the office and communicated through toolbox talks
All policies are reissued for acknowledgement following the annual review, whether or not changes have been made
Records retained as evidence

A digital acknowledgement register recording, for each member of staff: name, role, the pack version acknowledged, the date and time, and their signature confirming they have read and understood the policies
Toolbox talk records where policies have been briefed, including attendance signatures
A version control log showing the history of each policy pack, the changes made, and the Director's approval
How staff acknowledge this pack

Staff acknowledge the pack by signing the Company's acknowledgement register, digitally or on paper. Each acknowledgement records the date, the pack version and the signature given, and the register is available for inspection by clients and assessors.
